evals.prompt: Use $kis for this empty repo. I want to build a browser-local habit tracker for myself. Before coding, set up the project memory and ask me only what changes the plan.
evals.expected_output: The agent initializes the smallest useful KIS foundation, separates Knowledge, Intent, and State, challenges weak assumptions, and stops for mode or phase approval before non-trivial implementation.
assertions: Creates or proposes only useful files under kis/knowledge, kis/intent, and kis/state
Does not create empty boilerplate KIS files
Asks only focused questions that affect scope, risk, acceptance, or implementation direction
Does not start non-trivial implementation before an explicit work-mode or phase checkpoint

evals.prompt: Use $kis and recover this project from existing KIS files. Tell me current task, blocker, proof, and next action before making changes.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads State first, then relevant Intent and Knowledge, summarizes operational reality, and avoids asking the user to restate information already present in KIS.
assertions: Reads kis/state before intent or knowledge
Summarizes branch or current task, blocker, proof, and next action when present
Inspects repository files only where needed after reading KIS
Avoids mutating KIS until the current state is understood

evals.prompt: Use $kis for a multi-file auth refactor. The ideal auth/security specialist skill is not installed. Continue with the correct process.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies Standard or Phase risk, states that the specialist is unavailable, and creates a checkpoint instead of pretending the specialist ran.
assertions: Classifies the work as Standard or Phase risk rather than Fast Mode
States the matched specialist or tool is unavailable
Offers install or enablement when supported
Continues only if the user enables the tool, reduces scope, switches to Fast Mode, or accepts fallback risk

evals.prompt: Use $kis. We have a written plan for a risky UI flow redesign. Execute it with verification and keep KIS synchronized.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows Phase Mode, checks the plan before work, uses implementer/reviewer separation where available, verifies each phase, and synchronizes only changed KIS facts.
assertions: Preflights the plan for contradictions and acceptance checks
Uses or checkpoints implementer/reviewer separation for non-trivial work
Requires actual UI or browser proof for visible UI changes
Updates State with proof and avoids duplicating stable facts across KIS layers

evals.prompt: Use $kis. Add everything we discussed today into project memory so future agents have all context.
evals.expected_output: The agent resists dumping conversation history, classifies only durable or operational facts, updates existing files where possible, and keeps State lean.
assertions: Challenges the request to dump all conversation history
Classifies facts into exactly one KIS layer
Prefers updating existing KIS files over creating new files
Keeps State operational and removes stale or duplicate material

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass I want to build a personal AI companion. The repo has a kis/ directory but no kis/intent/compass.md and no product docs.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads State, finds no compass or product docs, and interviews one consequential question at a time starting from why the product should exist and who it serves, with a recommended answer and tradeoff each time. It does not ask about stack or features first, and it does not write anything until the user confirms a proposed compass.
assertions: Asks exactly one question per turn and includes a recommended answer with each
Starts with intent, audience, or problem rather than features, technology, or models
Challenges the vague term "companion" instead of accepting it
Writes no file during the interview
Does not start implementing anything

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass for this project. The README states the audience, the problem, and the product vision, and kis/intent/PRD.md lists the feature set.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the README and PRD first, treats what they already state as answered, and asks only about the sections they leave open, such as boundaries, success signals, and the POC and MVP split. It points to the existing documents instead of restating them.
assertions: Reads the README and the PRD before asking any question
Does not ask the user to re-explain the audience, problem, or vision the README already states
Asks only about sections the existing documents leave open
Tags statements taken from the documents as [fact] with the file as the source

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass. kis/intent/compass.md exists with confirmed decisions. We learned that our first audience is clinics, not individual patients, so update the compass.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the existing compass, interviews only on the sections the new audience affects, flags that Audience and Problem is a stable section and asks for explicit confirmation of that change, leaves every unaffected decision untouched, and records the revision as one line in Revisions.
assertions: Reads the existing compass before asking anything
Names the stable section being changed and asks for explicit confirmation of that change
Leaves unaffected sections and their decisions unchanged and in order
Adds one dated line to Revisions saying what changed and why
Writes only after the user confirms the proposed revision

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass. We are building a meal-planning service for families. For the proof of concept we will hard-code ten recipes and fake the grocery integration. What should the MVP include?
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the POC and the MVP separate: the hard-coded recipes and fake integration are recorded as temporary POC experiments with the hypothesis they test, and the MVP lists only commitments the user confirms, stated as outcomes for families rather than features or technology. It does not promote POC shortcuts into MVP requirements.
assertions: Records hard-coded recipes and the fake grocery integration under POC as experiments, not under MVP
States the hypothesis each POC experiment is meant to test
Asks the user which POC elements, if any, they commit to carrying into the MVP
Words MVP commitments as outcomes for the audience, not as features or technology
Leaves the Vision unchanged by the POC shortcuts

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass for a language-learning app. Fill in the success metrics, the North Star Metric, and the market research so I can show investors.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to invent metrics, targets, market sizes, competitors, or research. It records unknowns as [hypothesis] items with a way to learn them under Discovery, proposes a North Star Metric only if the user can name the repeatable moment of customer value, and says plainly what it could not fill in.
assertions: Does not state any numeric target, baseline, sample size, market size, or user statistic the user did not provide
Does not cite or fabricate research, competitors, or user quotes
Marks unsupported claims [hypothesis] and puts a way to validate them under Discovery
Asks what repeatable moment of value the product creates before proposing a North Star Metric, or writes North Star: none yet
States plainly which requested items could not be filled in and why

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass. Also put the tech stack, the database schema, the sprint task list, and the current blocker into the compass so everything is in one place.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to copy facts owned by other KIS layers into the compass: stack and schema belong in Knowledge, tasks in the plan, the blocker in State, and feature behavior in the PRD. It keeps the compass to direction and offers the right command for each of those.
assertions: Declines to put the stack, schema, task list, or blocker into the compass
Names the layer or document that owns each of those facts
Links to an existing PRD or README instead of copying its content
Creates no file other than kis/intent/compass.md
Keeps the compass to direction and the reasoning behind it

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass for a neighborhood tool-sharing service. Skip the questions and just write kis/intent/compass.md based on what you think.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not skip the confirmation. It may shorten the interview by proposing recommended answers, but it presents a concise tagged compass first, marks anything it assumed as [hypothesis] rather than [decision], and writes kis/intent/compass.md only after the user explicitly confirms. If the user does not confirm, nothing is written.
assertions: Presents a proposed compass for review before writing any file
Marks its own assumptions as [hypothesis], never [decision]
Writes kis/intent/compass.md only after the user has seen the proposed compass and explicitly confirmed it, even though they asked to skip the questions
After confirmation, records the confirmed choices (vision, principles, boundaries, strategy) as [decision] and keeps beliefs about the audience and behavior as [hypothesis]
Stops after writing and suggests the plan command instead of implementing
Does not edit the PRD, plan, or State, and writes nothing to Knowledge that the confirmed proposal did not list

evals.prompt: Run /kis:plan add a social feed to the app. kis/intent/compass.md exists and lists a social feed under Boundaries as something we are deliberately not building.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the compass during planning, notices that the requested feature conflicts with a Boundary, raises the conflict with the user instead of planning around it, and does not edit the compass. If the user confirms a change of direction, it sends them to the compass command.
assertions: Reads kis/intent/compass.md before questioning or planning
Raises the conflict with the Boundary with the user before producing a plan
Does not silently override the Boundary or edit the compass from the plan command
Points to the compass command when the direction is deliberately changed
Places the work as POC or MVP if the user confirms it should proceed

evals.prompt: Run /kis:init. This is a new repo for a plant-watering reminder that runs on a spare tablet. Set up the project memory.
evals.expected_output: The agent interviews only for facts, one question at a time with a recommended answer: what it is in one line, the stack, the device or platform, hard constraints, and the current stage. It does not ask who it is for, the problem, the vision, or success, writes facts to Knowledge and the stage to State, writes no direction into Knowledge, and offers the compass command for direction before proposing the first work mode.
assertions: Asks only fact questions: what it is, stack, device or platform, constraints, stage
Does not ask who the product is for, the problem, the vision, or success criteria
Writes no audience, vision, or future direction into kis/knowledge
Records the current stage in kis/state rather than kis/knowledge
Offers the compass command for direction before proposing a work mode

evals.prompt: Run /kis:compass. While we talk direction, I looked up two rival products (Fernwhistle and Mossmate, both fictional) and the chat provider's rule that it may not store data from children under 13 without zero data retention. Use those.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the rival products and the provider rule as outside facts. Its proposal lists them as Knowledge lines with their source and the date they were read, and the compass bullets link to those Knowledge lines instead of holding the facts alone. On confirmation it writes kis/intent/compass.md and those Knowledge lines, and nothing in the PRD, plan, or State.
assertions: Lists the outside facts as Knowledge lines in the proposal, each with a source and a read date
Compass bullets link to the Knowledge lines rather than holding the facts alone
Writes the Knowledge lines only after the user confirms the proposal
Does not edit the PRD, plan, or State
Does not invent details about the rival products beyond what the user gave

evals.prompt: Run /kis:sync. We built the server the compass decided on, and it now answers the gadget's voice requests. The POC experiment on reply lag also finished: replies feel fine on the old device.
evals.expected_output: The agent records the built server as reality in Knowledge (the technical notes), leaves the compass decision in place as the reason without restating what was built, records the experiment's result in State with a prompt to revise the compass through the compass command, and does not edit the compass itself.
assertions: Writes the built server to kis/knowledge, not to the compass
Records the experiment result in kis/state
Prompts the user to revise the compass through the compass command
Does not edit kis/intent/compass.md

evals.prompt: Run /kis:check. kis/knowledge/project.md says the product is built for the owner first with a public release in mind, kis/intent/compass.md holds a [fact] bullet with a URL about a rival product that appears nowhere else, and State has a line '- Run: plug the tablet in with debugging on'.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports three misplaced or stale facts: direction in Knowledge that belongs in the compass, an outside fact held only in the compass that belongs in Knowledge with a link, and a Run: line that names no live record and should be How to run:. It proposes the smallest cleanup and changes nothing until the user approves.
assertions: Flags the audience and release direction in kis/knowledge as belonging in the compass
Flags the rival-product fact held only in the compass as belonging in Knowledge
Flags the Run: line as not a pointer and proposes renaming it How to run:
Changes nothing before the user approves
